subject: general
question: Which of the following stages of an automatic transmission system locks the transmission, restricting a vehicle from moving?
solution:
The correct answer is __Park (P) stage.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Park (P) stage__ is a position in an automatic transmission system.
 
• When the vehicle is in the Park stage, the transmission locks the vehicle’s wheels, preventing it from rolling forward or backward.
 
• This stage is used when the vehicle is stationary and the driver wants to ensure it does not move.
 
• It is critical for parking safety, especially on inclines or uneven surfaces.
 
• The Park stage engages a parking pawl, a mechanical locking mechanism in the transmission system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Drive (D) stage:**

 
 
• Used to move the vehicle forward under normal driving conditions.
 
• It allows the automatic transmission to shift through all forward gears.
 
 
 
• **Neutral (N) stage:**
 
 
• Disconnects the engine from the wheels, allowing the vehicle to roll freely.
 
• It is often used when the vehicle is being towed or pushed.
 
 
 
• **Low (L) stage:**
 
 
• Provides increased torque for situations like climbing steep hills or towing heavy loads.
 
• Limits the transmission to lower gear ranges for better control.
